findings.problem: The chance bars stop halving at the last step: 1 in 8 and 1 in 16 are drawn the same width. A7.bar clamps the fill to at least 14 px plus its border, so the widths are 300, 150, 75, 42, 42 px. The scene's whole claim is 'each time the chance halves, one more bit', and in the final row (the one the caption 'Rarer news tells us more' lands on) the picture says the chance did not change.
findings.fix: Draw the chance as 16 equal blocks (one block = 1/16) and light 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 of them, so every halving is visible and exact; or give the fill no minimum width and widen BAR_W. Assert the rendered widths halve (A7.close on the 5 widths).
findings.evidence: s3@9.3 and s3@8: pixel scan of the blue fill gives x 242-283 for both '1 in 8' and '1 in 16' (see rows at y 694 and 802).

findings.problem: Caption 2 'Runs of one colour shrink into single codes.' contradicts the picture and is not how LZW works: no run becomes a single code (runs of 6, 3, 5, 4 pixels take 3, 2, 3, 3 codes). Row 1 is also labelled 'flat colour' although it shows four colours in runs, so a first-time learner reads 'flat colour' as 'what you see' and 'single codes' as run-length coding. (Same two issues as the facts review; from the learner's side they are the confusing words of the whole scene.)
findings.fix: Caption: 'Repeats need few codes: 18 pixels, 11 codes.' Label row 1 'a GIF row: long runs' (keep 'noisy' for row 2).
findings.evidence: s10@3.2 (caption over the 11 spans, 3 spans of 1, 2, 3 pixels under the six As) and s10@0.3 (label 'flat colour').

findings.problem: The decoder's learning rule is never shown where it is easy. 'Each code adds one entry to the table' plays over steps 2 and 3, but entries 2 = AB and 3 = BA just appear (s9@5.5, s9@6.8) with no sign of what they are built from. The rule 'previous + first letter of the current phrase' is only drawn once, for the odd case (code 4). A first-time learner meets the exception before the rule, and the caption's 'its first letter' is ambiguous (whose?).
findings.fix: Reuse the 3-slot equation (previous + first letter = new entry) for the first two codes, short and quick (A + B = AB, then B + A = BA), then hold on code 4 where the slot is a '?'. Caption for the trick: 'Code 4 is not in the table yet: it is AB plus AB's first letter.'
findings.evidence: s9@4.5 (code 1 read, dictionary still 0|A, 1|B), s9@5.5 (2|AB appears, only a small A flying), s9@7.8 (the equation shown for the first time).

findings.problem: The decision the whole scene is about is not drawn. Found lookups get a blue ring on the dictionary chip, but a failed lookup ('is AB known? no') shows nothing: A turns green, a code is sent and a new orange chip appears, and the caption has to explain why ('A new longer phrase: send a code, learn it'). A first-timer sees LZW do things without seeing the test that triggers them.
findings.fix: Show the candidate (phrase + next letter) as a small chip such as 'AB?' next to the orange next-letter ring, with the L5 tick (found, blue ring on the entry, keep growing) or cross (new: the sent chip flies and the orange entry is added). The cross should land just before the send.
findings.evidence: s8@2.5 (ring on B, nothing says AB is unknown), s8@3.5 (A sent, 2|AB added), s8@5.5 (the only visible lookup is the blue ring on 2|AB).

findings.problem: Handoff from Huffman to LZW is silent. Scene 7 ends on a code built from known chances; scene 8 jumps to a new method with only the kicker 'LZW'. The learner is never told why a second method exists or what is different (no chances needed in advance, no table sent). The first caption just describes the starting dictionary.
findings.fix: Make caption 1 carry the contrast: 'No chances needed: LZW learns as it reads.' (and keep the A and B dictionary visible as now).
findings.evidence: s7@11.8 to s8@1.2 (caption 'LZW starts with a tiny dictionary: A and B.').

findings.problem: The 'bits per letter' meter is the least understandable part of the scene. It is on screen from 0.6 s, before the tiles are explained, and the weights then fly into it (the meter goes 0.20, 0.49, 0.98, 1.98) with only the caption 'Its chance adds to the bits per letter.' That is true but nothing on screen says why a merge weight costs bits, so the bar reads as arbitrary bookkeeping and competes with the merge picture on the right of the stage.
findings.fix: Either show the reason (each merge pushes the letters below the new node one level deeper: pop a '+1 bit' on those leaves as the chip flies) and word the caption 'Letters under it pay one more bit.', or drop the meter until the tree is finished and then show the 3.00 / 1.98 / 1.96 bars once.
findings.evidence: s6@1 (meter labels and the grey fixed bar before any tile caption), s6@4.0 to s6@4.8 (0.00 to 0.20), s6@10.5 (1.48).

findings.problem: 'Floor' changes number without a word. Scene 4 teaches floor = 1.75 for the die; scene 6 ends on 'just above the 1.96 floor' for a different source, and the purple bar just says 'floor: 1.96'. A learner who remembers 1.75 will think one of them is wrong.
findings.fix: Label the purple bar 'floor for these chances: 1.96' (still 28 px) or say in the caption 'the floor for these chances'.
findings.evidence: s4@11.9 (floor 1.75) versus s6@12.5 (floor: 1.96).

findings.problem: The switch from the bad code (A 0, B 1, C 01) to the tree (A 0, B 10, C 110, D 111) is silent. B and C change, a new letter D appears, and the book tiles vanish. The viewer never sees the clash from the bad code on the tree (C hanging under the leaf of A), so 'put every code at a branch end' has no visible reason, and the new codes look like the same code redrawn.
findings.fix: Before the tree grows, add one short beat: tag 'a better code' (or a caption 'Fix it: a code that never starts another.'). Best: draw the bad code on the tree first (A at leaf 0, C passing through it, red), then slide C and add D to leaves.
findings.evidence: s5@4.5 (A0 B1 C01 and two readings) then s5@6.5 (tree with B 10, C 110, D 111, caption 'Put every code at a branch end.').

findings.problem: The surprise cells for the eight symbols pop in about 1.2 s (4.2-5.4), and the legend tile that 'lights up' for each symbol overlaps with the next ones (A and B, then A, B and C ringed together). At normal speed a first-timer cannot follow which legend tile gives which cells, which is the one mapping the scene needs for 'each one costs its surprise'.
findings.fix: Slow the reveal to about 0.3 s a symbol (4.2-6.6) and ring only the legend tile of the current symbol, one at a time; shift the gather, fixed-strip and average beats about 0.8 s later (there is room if the 1.6-2.8 legend pulse is cut).
findings.evidence: s4@4.4 (A and B ringed), s4@4.7 (A, B, C ringed), s4@5.3 (D ringed, all cells already there).

findings.problem: 'Floor' is only a tag, not a picture. 'the floor: none can beat it' appears at 10.0 as a purple pill; nothing on screen shows what cannot be beaten. The strips already carry the idea (fixed 16, surprise 14, entropy 14 / 8 = 1.75) but no limit is drawn, so the word floor is learned as a label rather than seen.
findings.fix: Draw a purple dashed floor line at the end of the 14th cell across the grey fixed strip (the two extra grey cells turn red: wasted), as the recap pictogram already does; keep the tag as the name of the line.
findings.evidence: s4@10 (tag over empty space, strips unmarked); compare s11@5.2 (the dashed floor line in the recap).

findings.problem: The finished 15-bit strip is drawn with gaps between codewords (1 1 011 010 001 1 000), straight after scene 5 insisted 'Codes sit side by side, with no gaps.' The learner never sees the real stream (110110100011000) or that it can be read back uniquely, so the payoff of scene 5 is not collected here.
findings.fix: In the last 1.5 s slide the groups together into one gap-free string of 15 cells (the blue underline can show the 7 codewords once), then count 15 vs 21. Same for the fixed strip if it shifts.
findings.evidence: s7@9 and s7@10.5 (green strip with gaps), s5@1.5 (no-gap received bits).

findings.problem: The payoff is only numbers. Both rows are 18 pixels and the result is two tags, '11 codes' with a green tick and '17 codes' with a red cross, so the saving is not seen as a size. Eleven of eighteen is not an obvious shrink next to seventeen of eighteen, which makes the title 'Repeats shrink' hard to believe at a glance.
findings.fix: Show the result as sizes: under each row a code strip of 11 and 17 equal cells against the 18-pixel row (or a short bar), so the first visibly ends before the pixel row and the second almost reaches it. Optionally choose a flatter row so the contrast is bigger.
findings.evidence: s10@5.2 (flat row: tag '18 pixels, 11 codes') and s10@9.5 (noisy row: '18 pixels, 17 codes').

findings.problem: '1 bit = one yes-or-no answer' is tied to the picture only by a tick and a cross beside a pill. The orange cells under 'surprise' are never shown to be yes-or-no questions, so the step from 'half the chance' to 'one yes-or-no answer' is asserted by the caption (2.8-5.0) rather than drawn.
findings.fix: When each new orange cell pops, put a tiny halving question on it (a split of the 16-block strip with a tick on the half that holds the news), or colour each cell with the tick or cross as it is answered.
findings.evidence: s3@3.5 (row 1 in 2 with one orange cell, key at the bottom left), s3@8 (four cells, still no link to the key).

findings.problem: Stage margins: the column headers sit at stage y 6, the row labels ('certain', '1 in 2', ...) at stage x 0, and the key's tick at x 9, all under the 12 px margin; the key also sits 12 px under the last row's lip, so the lower left is crowded while the right half of the lower stage is empty.
findings.fix: Re-space the ladder: headers y 12, labels x 12 (bars and cells +12 px), row pitch 104 instead of 108, key at y 584 (the 640 px stage then keeps 12 px at top, left and bottom).
findings.evidence: Playwright audit of s3@0.5 to s3@10.5 (bounding boxes: chance 170,6; certain 0,80; tick 9,590). Visible in s3@9.3 where the key hugs the 1 in 16 row.

findings.problem: Caption 3 'Noise rarely repeats, so almost nothing shrinks.' starts at 5.8, when the noisy row has only 3 tiles, and the result (17 codes) only shows at 8.4: the caption runs ahead of its picture for about 2.6 s. For the first 5 s the lower half of the stage is also empty (the figure sits in the top 25%).
findings.fix: Move caption 3 to about 7.4-9.2 so it lands with the 17 spans (8.4) and caption 4 to 9.3-10.6; start the noisy row's label and tiles earlier (about 4.0 s) so the lower half of the stage is not empty for the first 5 s.
findings.evidence: s10@5.2 (3 noisy tiles under caption window starting 5.8), s10@6.5 (4 codes, caption already says almost nothing shrinks), s10@3.2 (empty y 520-900).

findings.problem: The pixel palette (A green, B blue, C purple, D orange) reuses the video's role colours: the blue code spans sit under blue B pixels (they merge at x 392-538 in row 1), and green A pixels sit beside a red 'bad' tag. It is a documented exception, but it competes with the roles the learner has just internalised.
findings.fix: Give the code spans a neutral outline or grey, or use a distinct tone for the spans (for example grey with a dark lip) so they read as 'pieces', not as pixel colours.

findings.problem: 'fixed: 16 bits' appears without saying where 16 comes from, whereas scene 2 had a '3 bits each' tag. The pairs of grey cells hint 2 bits per symbol but a first-timer has to work out four symbols = 2 bits.
findings.fix: Add a grey '2 bits each' tag over the fixed strip as in scene 2.
findings.evidence: s4@8.7 (grey strip in pairs, tag 'fixed: 16 bits').

findings.problem: The decoded row shows nine empty slots from the start, so the decoder 'knows' the output length before decoding; it also leaves a tall empty band (page y 470-720) for most of the scene.
findings.fix: Grow the decoded row as letters arrive (a dashed slot only for the next letter), and tighten the empty band, or move the 'decoded' row up so it sits nearer the dictionary.
findings.evidence: s9@1.5 and s9@3 (nine dashed slots, empty middle band).

findings.problem: At the end A, B and C go green but D stays white, so the leaf D reads as not part of the code just as the 'prefix-free' tick lands. The tree also vanishes to a lone root node for about 0.4 s at the part 1 to part 2 change.
findings.fix: Turn all four leaves green with the tick (D last), and start the tree's root and first branches while the old rows fade.
findings.evidence: s5@10.8 (D still white), s5@5.8 (only a root circle on screen).

findings.problem: Row 1's pictogram leaves the tick floating about 130 px right of the dashed line, away from what it confirms, and the green strip stopping at a dashed line can be read as 'target length' rather than 'limit'. (The label wording 'no code beats it' is covered in the facts review.)
findings.fix: Pop the tick just right of the strips (about 20 px after the dashed line) and add a small purple 'floor' tag on the line (28 px minimum), so the line is named.
findings.evidence: s11@8.95 (tick at page x 410-455, strips and dashed line end at page x 300).
